system:
You are the Network operator and regulator reviewer, standing in for the telecom regulator and mobile operators (cell broadcast delivery). You check that the message can be delivered and read on a handset: required languages present, the length per language in cell broadcast pages, encoding, and that the first page carries the hazard and the action.
You see only each language's phone text with its character count, encoding and page count, and the profile's required languages. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

9.3.19.1 Identification of a directory number within a CBS-Message-Information-Page For information relating to this feature see 3GPP TS 23.040 [4]. 9.3.20 CBS-Message-Information-Length n This parameter gives the number of octets of the CBS-Message-Information-Page n containing user information. The remaining octets of the CBS-Message-Information-Page n contain only padding information and are not included in this parameter. In the case where the user information is encoded using the GSM 7 bit default alphabet and the last character terminates at an octet boundary, this parameter indicates the number of octets of user information. In the case where the last character does not terminate at an octet boundary, this parameter indicates the number of octets up to the octet boundary immediately following the last GSM 7 bit default alphabet character of user information. In UMTS and E-UTRAN, the CBS-Message-Information-Pages together with the associated CBS-MessageInformation-Length parameter are broadcasted as a single unit over the radio inteface, and are part of 'CB Data' parameter at the UE.

[FCC-FR-2025#0066] Wireless Emergency Alerts; Amendments to Part 11 (multilingual WEA implementation), Federal Register 2025-22434 (FR p.57296):
44. In this document, the Bureau adopts rules for multilingual templates that will increase the availability of Wireless Emergency Alerts (WEA) alerts for persons with limited English proficiency that understand one or more of the 13 most commonly spoken languages in the United States, as well as English and American Sign Language (ASL). This document requires Participating CMS Providers to support multilingual templates on mobile devices for the following eighteen alerts: tornado emergency, tornado warning, flash flood emergency, flash flood warning, severe thunderstorm, snow squall, dust storm, hurricane, storm surge, extreme wind, test alert, fire, tsunami, earthquake, boil water, avalanche, hazardous materials, and 911 outage. Participating CMS Providers are required to support pre-scripted alert templates for English, Arabic, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, French, German, Haitian Creole, Hindi, Italian, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, Tagalog, and Vietnamese. Participating CMS Providers are also required to support the inclusion of four fillable elements that allow for the customization of the pre-scripted templates. Further, Participating CMS Providers must cause the fillable English version of the pre-scripted alert message to accompany the alert messages that use the pre-scripted templates for written forms of the 13 languages. The alert message using the pre-scripted template in the non-English language must be displayed first, and must be followed by the alert message using the English pre-scripted template.

[TS23041#0421] 3GPP TS 23.041 Technical realization of Cell Broadcast Service (CBS), version 18.3.0 Release 18 (ETSI TS 123 041 V18.3.0) (p.84):
9.4.1.2.4 Page Parameter This parameter is coded as two 4-bit fields. The first field (bits 0-3) indicates the binary value of the total number of pages in the CBS message and the second field (bits 4-7) indicates binary the page number within that sequence. The coding starts at 0001, with 0000 reserved. If a mobile receives the code 0000 in either the first field or the second field then it shall treat the CBS message exactly the same as a CBS message with page parameter 0001 0001 (i.e. a single page message).

In the case where compression applies across multiple 'CBS-Message-Information-Page's, the compression header shall be present only in the first octet position of the first 'CBS-Message-Information-Page'. data.summary: Arabic and English are both present and the encodings fit the scripts. However, both versions far exceed the UAE one-page handset advice: English is 190 GSM-7 characters over 3 pages, and Arabic is 234 UCS-2 characters over 6 pages. Neither version carries a protective action, so page 1 states the hazard but tells the reader nothing to do. The drafter can fix both problems by rewriting much shorter texts that lead with hazard plus action.

objections.issue: Both language versions far exceed the UAE one-page limit. English is 190 GSM-7 characters across 3 pages, while a GSM-7 cell broadcast page holds 93 characters. Arabic is 234 UCS-2 characters across 6 pages. Readers would get split or partially displayed messages.
objections.fix: Rewrite each language to fit a single page. English should be 93 GSM-7 characters or fewer, with no extension-table characters. Arabic should fit in one UCS-2 page of about 41 characters. Drop the source line, put the dates in compact form, and keep only hazard, area, time and action.

evidence.quote: message should be limited to 1 page
The Message Information Page then consists of 93 user characters.

objections.issue: Neither the English nor the Arabic text contains any protective action. They describe the fog, the area, the time and the source, but give no instruction such as avoid driving or slow down and use low-beam lights. Page 1 therefore does not carry an action.
objections.fix: Add a short protective action in both languages within the first page. For example: 'Avoid driving; if you must, slow down and use low beams.' Give the action priority over the source attribution.

evidence.quote: coupled with a description of the threat and the protective action the public should take

no_basis.concern: The exact single-page capacity for UCS-2 Arabic text (about 41 characters in 82 octets) is very tight. A person may need to decide whether a multi-page Arabic message is acceptable if hazard plus action cannot fit. The clauses shown give 82 octets only for 8-bit data and do not state the UCS-2 per-page character count explicitly.
